tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description describes when to use the skill with explicit trigger contexts ('Use it when someone asks who can call Bedrock, wants to list or phase out long-term Bedrock API keys...'), focuses on user intents (auditing, triaging GuardDuty findings, checking guardrail gaps), explicitly lists many scenarios including implicit ones (how-to questions with no account), and excludes out-of-scope cases (AccessDenied, cost). It is dense but within a reasonable paragraph length and uses imperative phrasing ('Use it when...', 'Load it yourself...', 'Name every...', 'Never write...').
tests.evidence: "Audit Amazon Bedrock security, read-only - which IAM users and long-lived credentials can invoke models, and whether Bedrock Guardrails protect production. Use it when someone asks who can call Bedrock, wants to list or phase out long-term Bedrock API keys..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but focuses almost entirely on domain-specific, non-obvious policy (masking rules, check-id families, read-only constraints, area routing) rather than explaining general concepts the agent already knows. It does not waste space on generic explanations of IAM, Bedrock, or guardrails basics.
tests.evidence: Never write any 12-digit AWS account ID in full... Write `the account under review`, an audited account's IAM account alias, or `account ending NNNN`.
